description: Hello!!! I am Hari Havishey currently studying in 11th standard ,and I am very interested in topics like physics , astronomy and a little bit of coding. And I am creating a website where everyone can know and learn about the missions which have been abandoned due to various reasons, this will also help the new emerging space enthusiasts to know about the technology and hardware used to do these kinds of mission.
summary:
I built an interactive educational tool which will help the new people deciding to know about astronomy  which will help them know more about NASA's abandoned missions and the hardware used in them. There are a total of 17 abandoned missions in this webite, and my goal was not just to show the people about the missions conducted. I also wanted to teach how these hardware pieces are so important and are still held up to this day: even modern spacecraft and satellites also take these missions as a reference to complete their tasks. And I approached this challenge in a way: my goal was not only to provide information but to make it in a fun interactive way. The whole website is like a game. From the text to the fonts to how everything works, everything just feels like a game so the user is more engaged.

This is important because the people who are new to astronomy, or the people who want to learn about it, do not want to sit through lines and lines of information or pages and pages of information to get it. They are new to the hobby so they need to know in an entertaining way and my website does this exactly by making education and learning feel like a fun game instead of a chore.
details:
my project, Abandoned Not Forgotten, is an interactive educational tool that allows users to explore NASA's historical space missions and the hardware used in them across the solar system. Instead of just being a website with web pages with complex terms, I created it in such a manner that it is also fun and interactive. It takes the visitor on a visual journey beginning with a view of our solar system. They can see the 17 prestigious missions and study them. As I said, the website features 17 historical missions, which are considered some of the most important in NASA history. The users can select each enumerable mission and study it. After that, it will add up to the score, so you can see how many of the 17 missions you have studied at the end of the day. This project makes space exploration history more accessible to students and casual space enthusiasts instead of requiring visitors to navigate lengthy technical documents. It presents historical and scientific information through visual exploration, interactive storytelling, and knowledge-based activities. My primary goal is to encourage curiosity about space exploration and make it more engaging for the younger audience and the newer audience, so that people can develop an appreciation for engineering achievements behind the historical mission and understand how earlier people came up with solutions to such difficult tasks. The project we are developing uses:

  • HTML for the website structure and content
  • CSS for the visual design, responsive interface, animation, and transition
  • JavaScript for interactive elements, navigation, mission selection, search functionality, animations, and quiz logic

Python and all these are done in Visual Studio Code. Rather than presenting NASA's or historically important missions as a chronological timeline or an encyclopedia, I decided to approach it as an interactive journey through the method of human exploration. My central idea was to make these forgotten missions discoverable historical missions. The project also combines history, historical storytelling, with interactive knowledge assessment, allowing visitors to discover information and immediately test what they have learned. During the development, we considered several important factors:

  1. Target audience: the experience should be understandable and engaging for school-age students and casual space enthusiasts.
  2. The most important thing was scientific accuracy.
  3. Accessibility.
  4. Educational value.
  5. Visual storytelling.
